details.description: Universal-3.5 Pro is AssemblyAI's flagship pre-recorded (batch) speech-to-text model, built on an LLM-based decoder that AssemblyAI says targets higher accuracy on entities, rare words, and domain-specific terminology such as medication names and proper nouns. It supports 18 languages with native code-switching and automatic regional-dialect recognition, and AssemblyAI documents it as generally available. AssemblyAI positions it as the higher-accuracy option for the languages it covers, with the separate Universal-2 model handling additional languages outside that 18-language set.
advantages: AssemblyAI reports a mean word error rate of 5.6% (median 4.9%) on English test sets spanning 26 datasets, versus 6.1% for Universal-2 on the same sets.
On the multilingual FLEURS benchmark, AssemblyAI reports 4.58% WER versus 7.42% for Universal-2.
AssemblyAI reports 1.52% WER on LibriSpeech Clean and 4.87% WER on CommonVoice.
AssemblyAI reports a hallucination rate about 30% lower than OpenAI's Whisper.

Supports keyterm prompting for up to 1,000 custom terms (versus 200 for Universal-2) and, exclusively among AssemblyAI's speech models, general natural-language prompting for up to 1,500 words via the prompt parameter.

Includes a medical-domain tuning mode ('medical-v1') that AssemblyAI says reduces missed entity rates on pharmaceutical names and clinical terminology by about 20% for English, Spanish, German, and French.
disadvantages: Covers only 18 languages, versus Universal-2's 99+, so requests outside that set fall back to Universal-2.
Lacks Universal-2's native filler-word (disfluency) detection; AssemblyAI says similar behavior has to be achieved through prompting instead.
use_cases: High-accuracy transcription for medical scribes, sales intelligence calls, and meeting notetakers, per AssemblyAI.
Transcription requiring accurate recognition of entities such as phone numbers, emails, addresses, and medication names.
Multilingual audio with code-switching across the model's 18 supported languages.
Domain-tuned medical transcription via the model's Medical Mode.

notes: WER and hallucination-rate figures come from AssemblyAI's machine-readable model reference (assemblyai.com/llms/models.md); the dedicated docs page itself gives only qualitative accuracy claims. The 18-language list collapses regional variants named on the language pages (e.g. Global/US/UK/AU English; Metropolitan/Canadian/Belgian French; multiple Spanish and Portuguese variants) into one entry per language, matching AssemblyAI's stated count of 18. Facts carry no deprecation_date, consistent with AssemblyAI documenting this model as GA. Verify pass: corrected the hallucination-rate comparison to name Whisper specifically (AssemblyAI's own reference states '30% lower than Whisper', not 'competing solutions'); clarified that natural-language prompting is exclusive to this model rather than merely larger than Universal-2's; removed the 'mutually exclusive prompting' disadvantage after finding no support for it in the model's docs page, the API reference, or the keyterms-prompting guide; confirmed the medical-v1 name and ~20% figure on AssemblyAI's dedicated Medical Mode page.
